sources.title: Neuronal correlates of subjective visual perception
sources.role: Foundational single-unit recording study; perception-linked neurons in macaque STS during binocular rivalry
sources.key_finding: Neurons in superior temporal sulcus fire in relation to perceived motion direction, not physical stimulus

sources.title: The role of temporal cortical areas in perceptual organization
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
sources.role: Systematic comparison of V1-IT gradient in perception tracking during rivalry
sources.key_finding: V1 ~20% neurons track perception; IT cortex almost all neurons track perception; establishes perceptual fidelity gradient

sources.title: Neuronal activity in human primary visual cortex correlates with perception during binocular rivalry
sources.authors: Polonsky A, Blake R, Braun J, Heeger DJ
sources.role: Human fMRI evidence for V1 modulation during rivalry
sources.key_finding: V1 BOLD signal tracks perception at ~55% of physical alternation amplitude; V1-V4v all modulate similarly

sources.title: Neural bases of binocular rivalry
sources.authors: Tong F, Meng M, Blake R
sources.role: Review of dual-mechanism model; ventral stream suppression; information persistence
sources.key_finding: Binocular rivalry involves both low-level inhibitory and high-level excitatory mechanisms; suppressed stimuli leave adaptation aftereffects

sources.title: Hierarchy of cortical responses underlying binocular rivalry
sources.authors: Lee SH, Blake R, Heeger DJ
sources.role: Attention gates V1 competition to higher areas
sources.key_finding: V1 rivalry activity exists; attention is required for it to propagate to higher visual areas

sources.title: Role of mutual inhibition in binocular rivalry
sources.role: Computational analysis of mutual inhibition model vs Levelt propositions
sources.key_finding: Standard model violates Levelt L4 at low stimuli; recurrent excitation resolves this; two escape modes

sources.title: Can binocular rivalry reveal neural correlates of consciousness?
sources.authors: Blake R, Brascamp J, Heeger DJ
sources.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
sources.role: Critical examination of binocular rivalry as NCC tool
sources.key_finding: Four core concerns: inadequate controls, attention-awareness conflation, lack of generalization, correlation problem

sources.title: The 'laws' of binocular rivalry: 50 years of Levelt's propositions
sources.authors: Brascamp JW, Klink PC, Levelt WJM
sources.key_finding: Original propositions need modification; updated versions apply to broader bistable perception phenomena

sources.title: Binocular rivalry reveals an out-of-equilibrium neural dynamics suited for decision-making
sources.authors: Cao R, Pastukhov A, Aleshin S, Mattia M, Braun J
sources.role: Hierarchical bistable variable model; explains gamma distribution and sequential correlations
sources.key_finding: Rivalry follows hierarchical decision-making dynamics; dominance durations are gamma-distributed with scaling property

sources.title: Neural Dynamics during Binocular Rivalry: Indications from Human Lateral Geniculate Nucleus
sources.role: Human 7T fMRI of LGN M/P layers during rivalry
sources.key_finding: Both M and P layers show rivalry-correlated activity; LGN actively participates in competition, not just passive relay

sources.title: Does V1 response suppression initiate binocular rivalry?
sources.authors: Carlson BM, Mitchell BA, Dougherty K, Westerberg JA, Cox MA, Maier A
sources.role: Macaque V1 multi-electrode array; V1 suppression vs BRFS facilitation
sources.key_finding: Traditional rivalry shows V1 suppression; BRFS shows facilitation; adaptation is alternative trigger mechanism

sources.title: On the use of continuous flash suppression for the study of visual processing outside of awareness
sources.authors: Yang E, Brascamp J, Kang MS, Blake R
sources.role: Review of CFS methodology and unconscious processing findings
sources.key_finding: Semantic, affective and familiarity processing continues during CFS suppression; methodological guidelines provided
